intent_signal: Informational-to-transactional. Searchers want a plain-language definition of the DTV, then immediately drill into eligibility, the 500k THB funds proof, the 180-day stay/extension/tax interaction, and how to apply. Top SERP is split between official government pages (authoritative but thin/no-FAQ) and law/tax firms (deep but lead-gen framed). A consumer-friendly, soft-power/Muay-Thai-specific FAQ has clear room.
common_ground: DTV = 5-year multiple-entry visa, 180 days per entry
Three categories: Workcation, Thai soft power (Muay Thai, cooking, medical), Dependents
Financial proof of 500,000 THB (~USD 14,500-17,000) in bank statement
Apply online via official Thai e-Visa portal from outside Thailand
One in-country 180-day extension (1,900 THB) then visa run to reset
180+ days in a calendar year triggers Thai tax residency
Remote work for foreign employers allowed; no Thai work permit / no Thai clients

gap.description: No top result owns a comprehensive, consumer-friendly, filterable FAQ specifically for the Muay Thai / soft-power applicant. Official pages have no FAQ; law/tax firms bury answers in lead-gen long-form and skip the soft-power training angle, dependent specifics, and real-world denial/funds anxieties. A searchable FAQ page from a camp that actually files DTV soft-power dossiers can win the long-tail question cluster.

weakness: Government pages (rank 1 & 4) have zero FAQ and no extension/tax/re-entry guidance
Tax/law firm pages are lead-gen framed and US-tax-heavy, light on the soft-power/training applicant
Soft-power (Muay Thai) acceptance-letter pathway is mentioned but never explained in depth anywhere in top 5
Real applicant anxieties (denials, bank-statement seasoning, agent vs DIY) underserved by authoritative pages
No live-search / filterable FAQ UX exists in the top results
recommended_angle: Build /dtv-visa/faq as the only searchable, plain-English DTV FAQ that owns the soft-power Muay Thai pathway: answer the full eligibility/funds/180-day/tax/extension/family question cluster with an instant filter, lean on Wildcat's first-hand experience issuing soft-power acceptance letters and filing dossiers (real E-E-A-T the law/tax firms lack on the training angle).
